title: How to play chess in Telegram with Web3Chess
subtitle: Open the Mini App, choose a practice session, and understand player matches before committing a stake.
excerpt: Start chess inside Telegram: explore free A.I. practice, the Academy, opponent notifications, and the rules for USDT player matches.
takeaways: The chess client opens inside Telegram.
A.I. practice and puzzles are free.
Player matches use USDT stakes; withdrawals are a separate flow.

content.text: The appeal of chess inside Telegram is simple: your conversations and your board can share the same app. Web3Chess opens as a Mini App, so you can try the experience from a Telegram link.

Open Web3Chess and choose free A.I. practice. Get comfortable with moving pieces and watching the clock before choosing a player match. The Academy gives you another route into the game through lessons and tactical puzzles.
The bot can notify you when an opponent is found. Follow the current in-app instructions and return promptly when a match is ready. Closing a screen does not mean that an active game clock pauses.

Player matches use equal USDT stakes from platform balances. Read the current rules, eligibility and fees before confirming. In a decided match, settlement credits the winner’s platform balance; it does not promise an immediate transfer to a personal wallet.

A connected personal wallet and a Web3Chess platform balance serve different roles. A personal-wallet swap does not automatically fund the platform. Deposits require the network, token and reference shown in the app, and withdrawals follow their own confirmation steps.
Wager matches are 18+, subject to local availability, and you can lose your stake. Free A.I. practice gives you a way to learn without committing one.
